notes: Public cost examples mapped to confirmed smells. These are directional anchors from project research — not audited figures. Use to ground severity claims in the executive report.

2.cost_pool: Claim disputes, bad-faith exposure, class-action remediation

anchors.label: Labor depreciation class-action wave
anchors.description: A wave of class actions beginning around 2015 alleged that carriers were systematically depreciating labor costs when calculating actual cash value — a practice not disclosed or defined in policy language. One Trumbull/Hartford suit alone alleged more than $5 million in underpayments; industry-wide exposure has been estimated in the hundreds of millions.
anchors.dollar_figure: $5M+ in one case; industry-wide hundreds of millions
anchors.relevance: Directly tied to undefined ACV methodology — the same pattern flagged by SMELL2-H003.

anchors.label: State Farm ACV settlement
anchors.description: State Farm reached a $15.6 million settlement in a dispute over how actual cash value was calculated on property claims — a direct consequence of undefined ACV methodology in policy language.
anchors.relevance: ACV undefined in loss settlement conditions — the core SMELL2-H003 finding.

anchors.label: Kentucky ambiguity and bad-faith exposure
anchors.description: Project research (Pedicini example) shows that undefined payment terminology in Kentucky policy language has survived as the basis for bad-faith exposure. Kentucky courts treat policy ambiguity against the drafter.
anchors.dollar_figure: Bad-faith multiplier exposure — no single figure; materially increases dispute value
anchors.relevance: Kentucky-specific risk for carriers with undefined valuation terms in homeowners forms.

4.smell_name: Calculation Rule Drift / Unversioned Rate Reference
4.cost_pool: Systematic underpayment, premium leakage, audit findings

anchors.label: Marshall Fire underinsurance
anchors.description: A single home insured for $419,000 faced an $850,000 rebuild estimate after the Marshall Fire — a $431,000 gap driven by replacement cost estimates that were not synchronized with actual post-loss reconstruction pricing.
anchors.relevance: Unversioned rate or valuation reference that drifts from real-world cost — the SMELL4-H001 pattern.

anchors.label: Han v. State Farm
anchors.description: Alleged systematic property underpayment from using lower new-construction pricing rather than reconstruction pricing. Pattern affects entire claim population, not individual cases.
anchors.relevance: Filing cites an external manual without version — the filed promise and implemented method diverge.

5.cost_pool: Market conduct fines, remediation, refiling, interest and penalties

anchors.label: Florida OIR hurricane market conduct exams
anchors.description: Following post-hurricane market conduct examinations, Florida's OIR levied $2.575 million in fines across ten carriers. Findings included missing required notices, claim handling deadline failures, and payment timing violations — all traceable to regulatory mapping gaps in carrier filings.
anchors.relevance: Carriers with rate rules and mandatory coverage claims not anchored to regulatory authority are exposed to the same examination findings — the H004 and H005 patterns.

anchors.label: Louisiana hurricane market conduct exams
anchors.description: Louisiana proposed nearly $1 million in fines following hurricane claims examinations — the same pattern as Florida, driven by missing state-specific regulatory compliance in carrier claim handling.
anchors.relevance: Regulatory mapping gap in carrier filings — directly analogous to SMELL5-H004.

anchors.label: South Dakota Farmers/Foremost market conduct exam
anchors.description: A single property insurance market conduct examination produced a $750,000 penalty — establishing the low end of the documented fine range for regulatory mapping failures.
anchors.relevance: Low end of documented market conduct penalty range — establishes the floor for a single exam finding.

portfolio_framing.description: For a carrier with $1B+ in written premium, estimated annual impact ranges from the project's 10-year exposure analysis.
portfolio_framing.conservative_pitch: If the review has only a 10% chance of preventing a 1M-dollar remediation or litigation event, expected value is 100K. If the service costs 60K-90K, the buyer has a plausible positive expected ROI before counting reviewer time savings or reputational risk.
